name: Mississippi Delta soybean ground
headline: Fifty inches of rain, most of it when nothing is growing, and an aquifer falling under the summer pumps.
story: A 100-acre furrow-irrigated field east of Stoneville has grown soybeans every year on record. Soybeans leave little residue, so winter and spring storms fall on bare beds and carry soil and nutrients to the bayou. Summers are humid and hot, nights stay warm, soybean cyst nematode and herbicide-resistant pigweed build under one crop, and the alluvial aquifer that feeds the furrows is declining. Organic matter is low.

baseline_rotation.name: Continuous soybean, winter fallow

water_context.note: A cone of depression has formed in the central Delta. Surge valves, tailwater recovery and computerised hole selection are promoted to cut furrow losses.
